reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports a ~40-fold coercivity increase after RTA in FeCoNiMnCu and attributes it to anisotropic strain or directional order, but it does not claim L1₀ ordering occurs in the Pt-free film; the hypothesis overstates the evidence by asserting L1₀ ordering without Pt, which is not supported by the cited passages.
premises: RTA of FeCoNiMnCu thin films increases coercivity ~40-fold
Coercivity increase arises from magnetic anisotropy induced by anisotropic strain or directional chemical order
RTA can induce L1₀ ordering in related systems (e.g., FeCuPt)
The as-deposited film is chemically disordered with low coercivity (~10 Oe)
RTA at ~700–800 °C for 15 s under inert atmosphere will produce L1₀ ordering in FeCoNiMnCu
